channel.title: Six Strings App Articles (EN)
channel.description: Six Strings App blog and theory in English: rhythm, chords, fretboard, harmony, and practice.

item.title: What Is Musical Tension?
item.description: A clear explanation of musical tension: where it comes from, how it relates to keys, scale degrees, and chord functions, and why it often seeks resolution.

item.title: What Is the Tonic?
item.description: A clear explanation of the tonic: how it creates a sense of home, why it is not always the first note, and how to hear it in melody and harmony.

item.title: Major and Minor Pentatonic Scales
item.description: Learn the difference between major and minor pentatonic scales: their formulas, characteristic degrees, parallel and relative relationships, chord choices, and guitar applications.

item.title: What Is a Pentatonic Scale?
item.description: A clear explanation of the pentatonic scale: the formulas for major and minor pentatonic scales, how they are related, how to use them in improvisation, and how to find them on the fretboard.

item.title: Added-Tone Chords
item.description: A simple explanation of added-tone chords: what add2, add4, add6, and add9 mean, how they differ from sus and seventh chords, and how to use them in music.

item.title: What Are sus2 and sus4 Chords?
item.description: A simple explanation of sus2 and sus4 chords: why they do not contain a third, how they sound, and how they differ from major and minor chords.

item.title: What Is a Slash Chord?
item.description: A simple explanation of slash chords: how to read C/E, how slash chords relate to inversions, and how to use chords with a separate bass note.

item.title: What Is a Chord Inversion?
item.description: A simple explanation of chord inversions: what changes when the bass note is not the root, and how this affects harmony and voice leading.

item.title: Main Types of Seventh Chords
item.description: A reference guide to the main seventh chords: maj7, 7, m7, m7♭5, and dim7, with formulas, sound, and harmonic function.

item.title: What Is a Seventh Chord?
item.description: A simple explanation of seventh chords: how they are built from a triad plus a seventh, why they matter in harmony, and how to hear their tension.

item.title: Diminished and Augmented Triads
item.description: A simple explanation of diminished and augmented triads: formulas, sound, differences from major and minor, and practical harmonic use.

item.title: What Is a Musical Phrase?
item.description: A simple explanation of musical phrases: how a phrase differs from a motif, how it works in melody, and how to practise phrasing.

item.title: What Is Syncopation in Music?
item.description: A simple explanation of syncopation: how shifted accents work, how syncopation differs from a straight rhythm, and how to practise it by ear and on an instrument.

item.title: What Is a Musical Motif?
item.description: A simple explanation of a musical motif: how it differs from a phrase, how it works in melodies and riffs, how to develop a motif, and how to use it in a song.

item.title: Chord Function Trainer: How to Hear What a Chord Does in a Key
item.description: A personal story about why I built the Chord Function Trainer: to practice harmonic hearing, recognize chord functions, and understand how progressions move inside a key.

item.title: What Is Musical Ear?
item.description: A simple explanation of musical ear: what this skill is, what parts it includes, how to develop it, and why ear training matters not only for singers.

item.title: Minor Triad: The 1–♭3–5 Formula
item.description: A simple explanation of the minor triad: what notes it contains, why it sounds different from a major triad, and how to see the formula on the fretboard.

item.title: Melodic and Harmonic Intervals
item.description: A simple explanation of melodic and harmonic intervals: how notes played one after another differ from notes played together, how to hear the difference, and why it matters for musicians.

item.title: Major Triad: The 1–3–5 Formula
item.description: A simple explanation of the major triad: what notes it contains, how it sounds, how to see it on the fretboard, and how it differs from a minor triad.

item.title: What Is Groove in Music
item.description: A simple explanation of groove: how it differs from rhythm, tempo, and swing, what creates the feeling of motion, and how to start practising it.

item.title: How to Train Intervals by Ear
item.description: A practical guide to interval ear training: how to hear melodic and harmonic intervals, avoid guessing, and connect your ear to the fretboard.

item.title: Major, Minor, and Perfect Intervals
item.description: A simple explanation of interval quality: how a major third differs from a minor third, why fourths and fifths are called perfect, and how to see this on the fretboard.

item.title: Chord vs Fingering: What's the Difference
item.description: A simple explanation of the difference between a chord and a fingering: why the same chord can be played in different places on the fretboard and why guitarists need to understand this.

item.title: What Is an Arpeggio in Music
item.description: A simple explanation of arpeggios: how they differ from chords, picking patterns, and scales, and how to hear and play them on guitar.

item.title: Interval Ear Trainer: How to Train Your Ear with a Drone
item.description: Practice hearing intervals against a drone in Six Strings App: recognize distances between notes, develop your ear, and connect training with real music.

item.title: Major vs Minor: What Is the Difference
item.description: A simple comparison of major and minor: how the third and other scale degrees change, how to hear the difference in chords and keys, and how to see it on the guitar fretboard.

item.title: What Is Minor in Music
item.description: A simple explanation of minor in music: what minor chords, minor scales, and minor keys are, how to hear the minor third, and why minor does not always mean sad.

item.title: What Is Major in Music
item.description: A simple explanation of major in music: what major chords, major scales, and major keys are, how to hear the major third, and why major does not always mean happy.

item.title: What Is a Fretboard Position
item.description: A simple explanation of guitar fretboard positions: how they relate to hand placement, fingering, scales, and position shifts when playing phrases and riffs.

item.title: Microtone Trainer: How I Learned to Hear Guitar Bends and Intonation More Accurately
item.description: Why I built a microtone trainer for bends and intonation: two close pitches, instant feedback, and a simple way to transfer ear training to guitar practice.

item.title: Simple Intervals in Music
item.description: A simple explanation of intervals within one octave: how to count unisons, seconds, thirds, fourths, fifths, sixths, sevenths, and octaves, how to hear them, and how to find them on guitar.

item.title: Time Signature vs Tempo: What Is the Difference
item.description: A simple comparison of time signature and tempo: time signature groups beats into bars, while tempo shows the speed of the pulse. Examples in 4/4, 3/4, and 6/8.

item.title: What Are Strong and Weak Beats
item.description: A simple explanation of strong and weak beats: how to feel the support of a bar, how metrical position differs from accent, and how to apply this in guitar strumming and riffs.

item.title: Scale Identifier: How to Find a Scale from a Set of Notes
item.description: The Scale Identifier helps you find possible scales from a set of notes: useful for analyzing melodies, riffs, improvisation ideas, lessons, and fretboard practice.

item.title: What Is a Bar in Music
item.description: A simple explanation of bars in music: what a bar is, how it differs from a beat and a time signature, why bar lines matter, and how to count bars when playing guitar.

item.title: What Is a Rest in Music
item.description: A simple explanation of rests in music: why silence matters, how to count rests, how rest durations work, and how to practice rests on guitar.

item.title: Rhythm Generator: How to Practice Complex Patterns and Find Riff Ideas
item.description: How to use the Six Strings App rhythm generator for riffs, melodies, scales, and exercises: random patterns, different time signatures, quintuplets, sextuplets, and metronome practice.

item.title: What Is Fingering on Guitar
item.description: A simple explanation of guitar fingering: how finger choice connects to notes and chords, why the same phrase can be played in different ways, and how to choose a comfortable option.

item.title: How Triads Are Built
item.description: A simple explanation of triads: what a triad is, how it is built in thirds, how major, minor, diminished, and augmented triads differ, and how to see them on guitar.

item.title: What Is a Chord in Music
item.description: A simple explanation of chords: what a chord is, how it differs from a single note and a fingering, how chords are built from intervals, and why guitar players need them.

item.title: What Is a Key in Music
item.description: A simple explanation of musical keys: what a tonal center is, how a key differs from a scale, why the tonic matters, and how keys connect melodies, chords, and the guitar fretboard.

item.title: How to Build a Natural Minor Scale
item.description: A simple explanation of the natural minor scale: its whole-step and half-step formula, the example of A minor, how it differs from major, and how to see it on the guitar fretboard.

item.title: How to Build a Major Scale
item.description: A simple explanation of the major scale: how the whole-step and half-step formula works, how to build a major scale from any note, and how to see it on the guitar fretboard.

item.title: What Is a Scale Degree
item.description: A simple explanation of scale degrees: how to count notes inside a scale, why the tonic matters, how a scale degree differs from a note name, and how to see scale degrees on the guitar fretboard.

item.title: What Is a Scale in Music
item.description: A simple explanation of musical scales: what a scale is, how notes are ordered, why scale degrees matter, and how to see a scale on the guitar fretboard.

item.title: How to Memorize Fretboard Notes
item.description: A practical way to memorize notes on the guitar fretboard without rote learning: how to study notes in small groups, test yourself, and bring that knowledge into your playing.

item.title: Guitar Fretboard Basics
item.description: A simple explanation of the guitar fretboard: how strings, frets, notes, semitones, and octaves are connected, why notes repeat, and where to start learning the fretboard.

item.title: Song Builder: how cadences grew into a tool for progressions, structure, and groove
item.description: The Song Builder in Six Strings App grew from a simple idea: to hear cadences at different tempos, build chord progressions, generate song structures, and test harmony with a drum beat.

item.title: What Is an Octave
item.description: A simple explanation of the octave: why two notes can have the same name but sound higher or lower, how to hear an octave, and how to find it on the guitar fretboard.

item.title: What Is an Interval in Music
item.description: A simple explanation of intervals: what the distance between two notes means, how to hear an interval, how to see it on guitar, and why it matters for chords, scales, and melodies.

item.title: What Is a Time Signature: 4/4, 3/4, and 6/8 in Simple Terms
item.description: A simple explanation of time signatures for beginners: what 4/4, 3/4, and 6/8 mean, how to count beats in a bar, and how time signature differs from rhythm and tempo.

item.title: Chord Identifier by Fingering: how to find out what you are playing on the fretboard
item.description: A personal story behind the Chord Identifier in Six Strings App: how to find a chord name from a fingering, understand its notes, intervals, inversions, and use it when learning guitar parts.

item.title: What Is Note Duration
item.description: A simple explanation of note duration: how long a note lasts, how duration connects to pulse and tempo, and how to practice it in real playing.

item.title: Fretboard Explorer: why I built a tool for understanding the fretboard, not memorizing shapes
item.description: A personal story behind the Fretboard Explorer in Six Strings App: why chord shapes are not enough, and how notes, intervals, chords, and scales can help you understand the guitar or bass fretboard.

item.title: What Is Tempo in Music
item.description: A simple explanation of tempo: what BPM means, how tempo relates to pulse and rhythm, and how to train steady speed in practice.

item.title: What Is Pulse in Music
item.description: A simple explanation of musical pulse: how to feel a steady time support, and how pulse differs from rhythm and tempo.

item.title: What Is Rhythm in Music
item.description: A simple explanation of rhythm: how sounds and rests are placed in time, how rhythm differs from tempo, and how to practice it.

item.title: Tone and Semitone
item.description: A simple explanation of tones and semitones: how distances between notes work on guitar and why one fret equals one semitone.

item.title: What Is Pitch
item.description: A simple explanation of pitch: why some sounds feel higher or lower, and how to see that movement on the guitar fretboard.

item.title: Note Names: Do, Re, Mi and C, D, E
item.description: How solfege note names connect to the letter system C, D, E, why guitarists use letters, and what to learn first.

item.title: What Is a Note in Music
item.description: A simple explanation of a note: how a note differs from sound, why note names matter, and how to see notes on the guitar fretboard.

item.title: What Is Sound in Music
item.description: A simple explanation of sound in music: how music starts with sound, silence, and time before notes, rhythm, melody, and harmony appear.

item.title: Guitar strumming pattern library: how to find the right rhythm for a song faster
item.description: A guitar strumming pattern library with ready-made rhythmic patterns in different time signatures. Helps you preview options quickly, choose the right strumming pattern, and find ideas for practice and songwriting.

item.title: Online metronome for guitar practice: a mini drum machine for daily training
item.description: The Six Strings App online metronome helps you practice with more control and musical feel: customizable sound, progressive tempo mode, practice timer, genre-based patterns, flexible subdivisions, and saved custom rhythms.

item.title: What CAGED Is and How It Helps You See Chords Across the Fretboard
item.description: Learn what the CAGED system is, why it matters for guitarists, and how the Six Strings App tool helps you see chord shapes across the fretboard. Includes the origin story and practical first use cases.

item.title: Circle of Fifths: how to quickly understand relationships between keys
item.description: How to use the circle of fifths in practice: see relationships between keys, understand major and minor, choose chords, and make sense of harmony faster.

item.title: Harmony: how to see key chords, hear cadences, and understand modulations
item.description: An online tool for working with harmony: key chords, chord functions, cadences, and modulations with audio playback right in the browser. Useful for practice, arranging, and songwriting.

item.title: Rhythm Trainer for Guitarists: How to Develop Inner Pulse Through the Rhythmic Alphabet
item.description: What a rhythm trainer is, how it relates to Benny Greb’s rhythmic alphabet, and why it helps guitarists develop inner pulse, timing, and a stronger sense of rhythm.

item.title: Chords, Arpeggios, and Scales for Guitar, Bass, and Ukulele: A Tool for Practice and Improvisation
item.description: An online tool for finding chord fingerings, arpeggios, and suitable scales for guitar, bass, and ukulele. Useful for practice, improvisation, and song analysis. Six Strings App

item.title: Why I Created Six Strings App: From Personal Practice to an Open Project for Musicians
item.description: The story behind Six Strings App: how a personal project for rhythm, fretboard, chords, scales, harmony, and ear training grew into an open platform for musicians.
